about: The interior of the two ureters: each lumen, the muscular coat shown as ring swellings, the narrow places where a ureter is tightest, and the oblique passage through the bladder wall that acts as a one-way valve. It shows urine moving down each ureter in spaced boluses, as a wave of contraction pushes it. The wall layers are not drawn separately and the calibres and positions are schematic, not measurements.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Left Ureter
parts.summary: The tube carrying urine from the left kidney to the bladder
parts.function: The ureter runs down behind the abdominal cavity from the renal pelvis to the bladder. Urine does not simply drain through it: waves of contraction push small portions of it along. More urine from the kidney means the waves follow each other more closely, which you can see as shorter gaps between spurts.

drives.note: The more urine the kidney makes, the more the ureter has to carry.

parts.label: Right Ureter
parts.summary: The tube carrying urine from the right kidney to the bladder
parts.function: The right ureter does the same job as the left, on the other side of the midline. Each ureter has its own waves of contraction, and the two are not synchronised. It brightens as urine flow rises.

drives.note: The more urine the kidney makes, the more the ureter has to carry.

parts.label: Muscular Coat
parts.summary: Smooth muscle that squeezes urine along in waves
parts.function: The wall of each ureter contains smooth muscle that contracts in a wave, narrowing the tube behind a bolus of urine and driving it toward the bladder. This is peristalsis; it works even when the body is lying down. It is drawn as ring swellings along the tube.

drives.note: Stretching of the wall by more urine triggers more frequent waves of contraction.

parts.label: Narrow Points
parts.summary: Where the ureter is narrowest: at the pelvis and at the pelvic brim
parts.function: The ureter narrows where it leaves the renal pelvis and where it crosses the brim of the pelvis; the third narrow place is its passage through the bladder wall. These are the places where a kidney stone is most likely to lodge. They are drawn as collars around the tube.

parts.label: Vesicoureteric Junctions
parts.summary: The oblique entry into the bladder that works as a one-way valve
parts.function: Each ureter passes at a slant through the bladder wall. When the bladder fills or squeezes, the pressure flattens that slanting passage and prevents urine from running back up toward the kidney, while an arriving bolus of urine can still push through. In the simulation the junction opens as a bolus arrives and relaxes shut between boluses.

drives.note: Each arriving bolus of urine opens the junction, so more urine means more opening.
A fuller bladder presses harder on the slanting passage, working the valve more.
